newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 25.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Say sorry MP tells Aussie 'mongrels': The government's diplomatic mask over leaked Australian Government papers slipped on Thursday as Prime Minister Jim Bolger and Treasurer Winston Peters prepare to tackle their Canberra counterparts in Melbourne on Saturday. Page 1.
Kirton's job comes under double scrutiny: NZ First minister Neil Kirton's tasks in the health portfolio are under review by Prime Minister Jim Bolger and Health Minister Bill English. Page 1.
Birch blames media for 'will they, won't they' super, tax-cut confusion: Finance Minister Bill Birch on Thursday blamed the media for the government's confusing signals on future tax cuts. Page 2.
Credibility of defence force questioned: New Zealand did not have a credible defence force, Foreign Affairs and Trade Ministry deputy secretary Neil Walter said on Thursday. Page 2.

Clark to represent Alliance's place: Labour leader Helen Clark will represent the Alliance on the privileges committee when it considers whether newly independent MP Alamein Kopu should remain in Parliament. Page 2.
Dairy exports push surplus to $150m: Dairy product exports boomed by $530 million in the pst June year to more than $3.5 billion, latest trade figures show. Page 13.

Saturn partner helps fund new system: Saturn Communications has brought in a partner, Canadian telecommunications company SaskTel, to share the costs of a $130 million telecommunications network for the Wellington area to be completed in the next two years. Page 13.

Let agents sell -- president: Real estate agents should get on with the business of selling houses and let lawyers do the conveyancing, according to Real Estate Institute president Colin Brown. Page 13.

Luxton has concern on super plan: The high rate of home ownership could fall by half if the compulsory retirement savings scheme referendum succeeded, Commerce Minister John Luxton said on Thursday. Page 13.
THE PRESS

Insults fly over Aust leaks: "Dingoistic", a pack of mongrels, clumsy imbecile -- those were terms used by senior New Zealand ministers as the Australian briefing papers row heated up on Thursday. Page 1.
Govt to pay heart unit 'shortfall': The full costs of Christchurch's heart unit should be borne by the taxpayer, says Health Minister Bill English. Page 1.
Tribe claims Beehive land: The land on which Parliament stands is included in a new Maori claim, because the claimants say it was "stolen". Page 2.
NZ dollar fall likely to help CHH: Carter Holt Harvey expects that the sharp drop in the New Zealand dollar since the end of June will boost its annual result. Page 25.
BNZ posts 15 pct profit increase: Bank of New Zealand on Thursday posted a 14.8 percent increse in operating profit, after tax and minorities, to $264 million for the nine months to June 30. Page 25.
Red ink still plagues Fletcher Forest plant: Weak prices for Japanese housing componentry have hit Fletcher Challenge Forest's Kawerau laminating plant. Page 25.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Free teenage dental visits under threat: Many dentists, fed up with fighting the government year after year to cover their costs, have already pulled out of the underfunded free dental scheme. Others threaten to follow suit.

Back-out option for Britomart investors: Investors in the Britomart redevelopment company Pacific Capital Assets will have the novel option of backing out of their commitment if the project does not go ahead as scheduled.
Sky plans tourism deal: Sky City and Tourism Holdings are in negotiations over a possible joint venture which could tie together the Sky Tower, Kelly Tarlton's underwater world and the Waitomo Caves.
Mercury pushes for vote: Mercury Energy will ask the High Court to force Power New Zealand to hold a shareholders' meeting to vote on a change of directors.
BIL sells FCL Energy stake: Brierley Investments has sold its Fletcher Energy holding in a move estimated to have netted the corporate raider a slick $26 million profit.
Hong Kong company buys Sheraton Hotel for $90 million: Auckland's Sheraton Hotel & Vowers has been sold by the Nauru Government to a Hong Kong listed company for slightly more than $90 million.
